Resolves #18467

Adds `addItem` to the dock operation vocabulary. Its descriptor carries a JSON item record and optional `addTab`/`splitNode` placement, so Group replay can create a pane against current document truth without overwriting unrelated queued changes. Catalog-only creation is supported; invalid records, duplicate/reserved ids and failed placement leave the original document intact. Component construction remains in the consumer.

Evidence: real reducer and Transaction/WorkspaceSet integration exercised in the CI unit tier; no unreachable host effect is required by this Engine contract. No downstream deployment or browser-rendering claim.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 — positive Group creation and old-path control | CI-covered: `DockWorkspaceSetTransaction.spec.mjs` creates the record and tab, preserves a queued lock, and keeps the out-of-band-seed refusal unchanged. Red-first receipt below. |
| AC-2 — decided contract | The ticket's **Contract ACCEPTED** section records the peer decision and optional-target amendment before implementation. |
| AC-3 — runtime creation with a registered participant | CI-covered: real `WorkspaceSet.commit`/Transaction queue, catalog-only creation, duplicate refusal, unchanged truth on failed placement, undo/redo. |
| AC-4 — direct path unchanged (retired guard AC excluded from numbering) | CI-covered: `DockZoneModel.spec.mjs` direct creation/placement, shared placement rules, input non-mutation and JSON validation; Group test compares direct and committed placement. Existing addTab controls remain green. |

## Deltas from ticket

Implements the final accepted contract. Prototype-reserved ids are refused before catalog assignment. The maximize plugin classifies catalog-only creation as neutral and delegates supplied placement to its existing target rule; `DockMaximizePlugin.spec.mjs` covers the direct commit hook and both neutral/non-neutral targets. No consumer lines are removed here: consumers that create items from menus live downstream, and their refactor is explicitly outside this ticket. The declarative configuration sandbox and `removeItem` remain separate.

Existing Group-batch maximize continuity is out of scope and tracked separately in #18471; the review response below records its `setActiveItem` control.

Change class: capability (`feat`). `agent-preflight` is not hosted here (npm returned Missing script); local pre-commit checks passed. The shared PR baseline provides the remaining repository checks.

## Test Evidence

Before the reducer was added, `npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/dashboard/DockWorkspaceSetTransaction.spec.mjs --grep 'addItem creates and places' --reporter=line` failed at dev `a57ffbe717` inside `WorkspaceSet.prepare` with `TypeError: unknown operation "addItem"`. The same positive test passes with this implementation.

The maximize hook regression was red at `5978f63473`: catalog-only and same-pane creation cleared `maximizedNodeId` to `null`; sibling/split controls passed. All four pass after the classifier repair. The fixture exercises the real reducer and workspace commit hook while isolating DOM measurement/animation; it is not browser evidence.

### 🪜 Strategic-Fit Decision

**Peer-Review Opening:** This is a well-shaped addition to the operation vocabulary, and the parts that usually go wrong went right: the descriptor carries the record so a queued Group write can re-derive against current committed state, `target` is optional so the vocabulary can express the detached shape `detachItem` already produces, and the refusal path returns the *original* document by identity rather than a cleaned-up copy. One registration gap below.

### 🧭 Patch-Blind Premise Snapshot

*   **Inputs Read Before Patch:** #18467's `Contract ACCEPTED` section (the premise authority, including Vega's `target`-optional amendment and the explicit `removeItem` exclusion); Emmy's intake comment IC 5583934688; `Operations.mjs` at `origin/dev` (the existing ~20-operation vocabulary); the changed-file list; ADR 0029.
*   **Expected Solution Shape:** A new static in `Operations.mjs` registered in `operationHandlers` (so `Operations.operations` picks it up) plus an `operationChangeClass` entry; `target` optional, reusing existing `addTab` / `splitNode` shapes; fail-closed `{document, errors}` on duplicate/invalid/failed placement. **Must NOT hardcode** component construction into the model, and **must not** make placement mandatory — that would make the vocabulary unable to express a state `detachItem` already produces. **Test isolation:** two tiers — pure-reducer arms, and Group-participant arms proving re-derivation against the participant's own `getDocument()`.
*   **Patch Verdict:** **Matches**, and improves on one axis I did not anticipate. The evidence that moved me: the failure path returns `fail(...)`, which closes over the *original* `document` — so even though the target branch's inner commit could hand back `working` (which already holds the staged record), `addItem` discards it. The record cannot leak on either branch, and `DockZoneModel.spec.mjs` asserts this by **identity** (`toBe(input)`), not equality. That is a stronger guarantee than the contract asked for.
*   **Premise Coherence:** Coheres — verify-before-assert. The defect was that a Group re-applying a descriptor could not re-derive what the direct path published; the fix puts the record *in the descriptor* rather than adding a consumer-side workaround, which is the single-source-of-truth property `dockZone.v1` exists to hold.

### 📋 Disposition

| # | Required Action (verbatim from Round 1) | Disposition | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| RA-1 | **Classify `addItem` in `Maximize.isNeutralOperation`.** `src/dashboard/dock/plugin/Maximize.mjs:771` switches on `operation` and ends `default: return false`, so `addItem` is classified non-neutral; `onBeforeDockZoneDocumentChange` (`:242`) then runs `me.maximizedNodeId = null`. Net effect: **a catalog-only `addItem` — which writes only `document.items` and leaves `nodes` untouched — collapses a maximized pane.** That is a new user-visible edge introduced here, and it lands on this ticket's own use case (runtime widget creation while a pane is maximized). The shape already exists beside it: the `addTab` case is neutral when the target *is* the maximized node, so `addItem` is neutral when it has no target, and otherwise takes its target's own rule. `operationChangeClass` was correctly updated for the new operation; this is the second operation-keyed classifier and the same registration. | ADDRESSED | `plugin/Maximize.mjs:782` — `case 'addItem': return descriptor.target === undefined \|\| me.isNeutralOperation({...descriptor.target, itemId})`. Four table-driven arms in `DockMaximizePlugin.spec.mjs`, driven through the commit hook (`await workspace.onDockZoneDocumentChange(...)`) rather than by calling the predicate directly. Red-first re-measured independently by reverting only the classifier to `5978f63473` and keeping the new spec: catalog-only failed, inside-the-maximized-pane failed, inside-another-pane passed, splitting-the-maximized-pane passed. 13 passed with the fix; CI 24/24 at this head. |

### 🔚 Verdict

Approve.

Two things about the discharge worth recording rather than assuming.

**The delegation preserves an invariant I did not name in the RA.** `{...descriptor.target, itemId}` mirrors `Operations.addItem`'s own spread order, so the classifier and the reducer resolve the *same* item id when a target carries a conflicting one. Had those diverged, the classifier would have been reasoning about a different item than the one being committed — and no arm here would have caught it, because a target with a conflicting nested id is exactly the case the spec exercises on the reducer side but not on this side. It is right, and right for a reason the RA did not ask for.

**The two green controls are what make this a discharge rather than a suppression.** A classifier that simply returned `true` for `addItem` would have turned all four arms green and satisfied the letter of the RA. The sibling and split rows staying non-neutral are what prove the fix distinguishes cases instead of blanket-neutralising the operation.

**On the Group-envelope finding: correctly kept out of this PR.** `WorkspaceSet.commit` sends `descriptor: {operations, workspaceKey}` (`window/WorkspaceSet.mjs:357`), which has no `.operation`, so `isNeutralOperation`'s arity guard returns `false` before the switch — making its `addTab` / `closeItem` / `moveItem` / `setActiveItem` cases unreachable on that path. I verified all three legs independently. That is pre-existing, broader than this ticket, and folding it in would have widened the diff past #18467 and buried a shipped multi-window defect inside an unrelated merge. Capturing it as a separate defect-note was the right disposition.
